$comment: ADR-0186 T / ADR-0177 row 19. HAND-WRITTEN from Phoenix's public documentation. The Phoenix server is Elastic License 2.0: no Phoenix code is copied, depended on, bundled or hosted. A customer may point our OTLP export at their own Phoenix; that is the only relationship.

Sources, opened 2026-10-07 (HTTP 200, quoted text confirmed on each published page): https://arize.com/docs/phoenix/tracing/concepts-tracing/otel-openinference/span-kinds, .../otel-openinference/resource, .../otel-openinference/exporter, and https://arize.com/docs/phoenix/release-notes/05-2026/05-15-2026-otel-semconv-conversion; read in full from their docs source, github.com/Arize-ai/phoenix @ 3383f07731f1f26ef758ecf49ee1eae9c7e0ef3d (2026-10-06), docs/phoenix/...

TRANSPORT is the one rule NOT from a docs page: the docs say the HTTP exporter defaults to http/protobuf but never say JSON is refused. That fact was read (not copied) from the server's own route declaration, src/phoenix/server/api/routers/v1/traces.py at the same commit, whose response description reads: 415 'Unsupported content type (only `application/x-protobuf` is supported)'. Interop fact, VERIFIED at that commit; it is not in the published docs.

Finding recorded by this fixture: our exporter sends OTLP/HTTP JSON only, so Phoenix cannot take our export directly. It needs an OpenTelemetry Collector between us and it (an otlp receiver on HTTP/JSON, an otlphttp exporter on protobuf). The attribute rules below are what Phoenix keys on once the Collector has re-encoded the same spans; the OTLP JSON and protobuf encodings carry the same data.

transport.via: an OpenTelemetry Collector: otlp receiver (http, JSON) -> otlphttp exporter (protobuf) to http://<phoenix>:6006/v1/traces
transport.doc: Phoenix serves OTLP/HTTP on port `6006` ... Point the exporter at `http://<host>:6006/v1/traces` (exporter.mdx); server route: 415 'only `application/x-protobuf` is supported'

span.doc: The OTLP/HTTP JSON encoding the Collector re-encodes (lowercase hex ids, fixed64 nanos as decimal strings). Timestamps are nanoseconds: 19 digits for any date from 2001 to 2286, so a millisecond or second value fails.

resourceAttributes.doc: `openinference.project.name` resource attribute | Canonical | The name of the project in Phoenix ... Forgetting to set a project name — ... spans land in the default project

everySpan.doc: Span kind is set via the `openinference.span.kind` attribute. **The value is ALL CAPS** ... A span without that attribute renders with a blank icon.

everySpanOfASession.doc: Common Attributes Across All Kinds: `session.id` Groups traces into a session; `user.id` The user the request belongs to.

tool.doc: TOOL: A call to an external tool, API, or function on behalf of an LLM.

policy.doc: GUARDRAIL: A validation of LLM input or output for safety, policy, or compliance.

llm.doc: Release note 2026-05-15 (arize-phoenix 15.10.0+): `gen_ai.input.messages` -> `llm.input_messages.*`; `gen_ai.usage.*` -> `llm.token_count.prompt`, `llm.token_count.completion`; `gen_ai.system` / `gen_ai.request.model` -> `llm.provider`, `llm.model_name`; `gen_ai.operation.name` -> `llm.invocation_parameters`. The note names `gen_ai.system`; the provider rule also accepts `gen_ai.provider.name` because the converter reads it first (seen in the same commit, src/phoenix/trace/gen_ai/conversion.py, `_resolve_provider_and_system`: `gen_ai.system` is read only when `gen_ai.provider.name` is absent).
